subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; exact module variant unresolved here.
subsystems.intake: Sensor-triggered station funnel closes after coral entry; compact extending algae roller fits around existing mechanisms.
subsystems.transfer: Funnel hands coral to effector; roller feeds ground algae to claw.
subsystems.scoring: Elevator/arm positions shared scoring assembly at L1–L4, processor and net.
subsystems.endgame: Gas-shock deployment, grappling hooks and forward-drive cage engagement; tipping contact activates switches before string winch lifts.
subsystems.controls: Three Limelight 4s; automatic reef alignment and current-aware algae holding voltage.

versions: Climb geometry simplified during prototyping after observing natural cage engagement; centering was repeatedly revised.
Interview shows NE DCMP configuration; earlier robot versions require further reconstruction.
dossier.analysis: Sensing the physical capture before winching is more valuable than assuming a nominal driver position guarantees engagement. The compact algae addition shows how extra points can be added without replacing the entire primary scorer.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2025-190 · Funnel closure and adaptive grip are separate control problems
context_documents.body:
# 2025-190: Funnel closure and adaptive grip are separate control problems

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A retroreflective beam across the station funnel detects entry and triggers closure before coral rolls to the end effector. An extending roller acquires ground algae. The retained scoring assembly uses an elevator and arm; the climb deploys with a gas shock and captures the cage while the robot advances.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The interview describes varying algae-holding voltage using current-related feedback, with more effort when the piece is farther out and less after it is seated. Exact thresholds are not supplied.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

An entry beam establishes interruption, not orientation or secure final possession. The handoff therefore needs additional state and a recovery path. Adaptive grip can reduce unnecessary loading after capture, but current also changes with friction, compression and voltage; it cannot be treated as a direct position measurement without calibration. The gas-shock climb similarly depends on a defined hard stop and a controlled chassis approach.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Induce partial entry and bounced coral, measure algae retention at different compression and current, and verify cage capture over realistic lateral offsets.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
